candidates.title: Newborn Screening for X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy: A Systematic Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) is the most common leukodystrophy and peroxisomal disorder. It was added to newborn screening (NBS) programs following its first implementation in New York in 2013. Since then, X-ALD screening has expanded rapidly, although important differences exist among programs. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the global implementation of NBS for X-ALD, including screening methodologies, screening performance, prevalence estimates, genetic findings, and clinical follow-up outcomes. A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE identified 13 publications describing NBS programs conducted between 2013 and June 2026. All programs used C26:0-lysophosphatidylcholine (C26:0-LPC) as the primary biomarker, although substantial heterogeneity was observed in analytical methodologies, cut-off values, screening algorithms, and follow-up strategies. Positive predictive values ranged from 9.1% to 100%, while screening detection rates varied from 1:3118 to 1:51,081, reflecting differences in study design, screening population, sample size, and screening approaches. Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) accounted for 52.6% of individuals detected with classified ABCD1 variant findings, representing a major challenge for genetic counseling and clinical management. Most identified newborns were asymptomatic at diagnosis, supporting the role of NBS in enabling early surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and cerebral disease before irreversible manifestations occur. In addition, differences between universal and sex-specific screening strategies highlight ongoing clinical and ethical debates regarding the scope of X-ALD NBS. Overall, current evidence supports the feasibility of NBS for X-ALD and its ability to enable presymptomatic ascertainment and early clinical surveillance; however, greater harmonization of screening protocols, improved variant interpretation, and long-term outcome studies are needed to optimize program performance and clinical benefit.

candidates.title: Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment of Gingival Metal Tattoo Using Optical Coherence Tomography and Er:YAG Laser-Assisted Microsurgery: A Case Series with an Ex Vivo Proof-of-Concept Study.
candidates.abstract: Background: Gingival metal tattoos caused by prosthodontic treatment present esthetic problems. To date, their removal has been unpredictable because of invasive surgical methods and the lack of reliable diagnostic tools. Objective: This study investigated the potential utility of optical coherence tomography (OCT) for the non-invasive assessment of metal tattoos and evaluated the minimally invasive removal using Er:YAG laser microsurgery. Methods: This study comprised an exploratory ex vivo proof-of-concept experiment using three gingival metal tattoo models and a clinical case series of three patients with gingival metal tattoos. Ex vivo models were created using porcine gingiva with artificially embedded metal fragments, which were analyzed through OCT and histological examination. In the clinical cases, three women with anterior gingival metal tattoos underwent OCT followed by Er:YAG laser microsurgery under microscopic guidance between 2012 and 2013. Results: Ex vivo experiments showed highly reflective OCT signals corresponding to the histological locations of metal fragments within the connective tissue. Clinically, OCT enabled visualization and localization of findings consistent with metal fragments and provided guidance for Er:YAG laser removal. All three patients showed uneventful healing without postoperative pain. Follow-up was available for 1.5 months in Case 1 and for up to 13 years in Cases 2 and 3, with favorable long-term clinical and esthetic outcomes observed in the latter two cases. Conclusions: OCT may facilitate non-invasive assessment and localization of gingival metal tattoos. When combined with Er:YAG laser microsurgery, it may provide a feasible and minimally invasive approach with favorable esthetic outcomes.

candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery-A Narrative Review.
candidates.abstract: Background: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly growing in the field of dental medicine and in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS). The aim of the present review is to assess current applications of AI in OMS, to evaluate their advantages and limitations, and to identify areas requiring further research. Materials and Methods: A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, with targeted keywords including "artificial intelligence," "deep learning," "machine learning," "oral surgery," "maxillofacial surgery," and "diagnosis "Artificial Intelligence" OR "Machine Learning" OR "Deep Learning" AND "Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery" OR "Oral Surgery" OR "Maxillofacial Surgery" AND "Diagnosis". Of 308 identified studies, 37 met the inclusion criteria focusing on AI-assisted detection interpretation and surgical planning in OMS. Results: AI is effective in identifying anatomical landmarks, evaluating lesions and cysts, diagnosing bone disease like medication-related osteonecrosis of jaws (MRONJ), planning dental implants, and aiding in the classification of fractures and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. AI can match or outperform human experts in various diagnostic tasks, particularly in panoramic and cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) image analysis. AI shows promise in early detection of impacted and supernumerary teeth, maxillofacial pathologies, neoplastic conditions, and soft tissue calcifications. Limitations: However, substantial methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent reporting of AI performance metrics, and limited external validation across the included studies constrain direct comparison of results and assessment of the generalizability of reported AI performance. Conclusions: AI may assist clinicians in diagnostic and treatment-related decision-making, but current evidence does not support its use as a replacement for comprehensive clinical assessment and professional judgment.

candidates.title: Early Clinical Outcomes of a Simplified Guided Single-Implant Workflow for Mandibular Overdentures: A Prospective Translational Proof-of-Concept Study.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: The present study evaluated the early clinical outcomes and translational proof-of-concept of a simplified guided single-implant workflow for mandibular overdenture rehabilitation in edentulous patients. Methods: A prospective translational clinical pilot study was conducted in 15 edentulous patients treated using a simplified flapless guided single-implant mandibular overdenture protocol. The workflow was designed to reduce procedural complexity while maintaining clinically applicable surgical and prosthetic integration under routine treatment conditions. All surgical procedures were performed by a single experienced operator. The study was conducted following institutional ethical approval and informed consent procedures. Clinical, radiographic, peri-implant, prosthetic, and patient-reported outcomes were evaluated during the 1-year follow-up period. Marginal bone loss, peri-implant clinical parameters, complications, implant survival, and Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14) scores were assessed. Results: All planned surgical and prosthetic procedures were completed successfully, with no major intraoperative or protocol-related complications. Implant survival was 100% during the 1-year follow-up period. Mean marginal bone loss was 0.19 ± 0.21 mm at loading and 0.25 ± 0.28 mm at 1 year. Peri-implant clinical parameters remained favorable throughout follow-up. Significant improvement in patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes was observed, with OHIP-14 scores demonstrating substantial reduction following treatment (p < 0.001). The simplified guided approach demonstrated favorable translational feasibility and practical clinical integration under routine treatment conditions. Conclusions: Within the limitations of this prospective translational clinical proof-of-concept study, the proposed simplified guided single-implant workflow demonstrated encouraging early clinical, radiographic, and patient-centered outcomes for mandibular overdenture rehabilitation. Further multicenter investigations involving larger patient cohorts, multiple operators, longer follow-up periods, and comparative study designs are required to evaluate long-term clinical performance, reproducibility, and comparative effectiveness relative to established treatment protocols.

candidates.title: Prevention and management of hormonal crisis in neuroendocrine tumors undergoing PRRT (peptide receptor radionuclide therapy): a systematic review.
candidates.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is an established treatment of advanced well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) expressing somatostatin receptors. Although generally well tolerated, PRRT may precipitate or exacerbate pre-existing hormonal syndromes in patients with functioning NETs, leading to acute endocrine decompensation requiring urgent management. Current recommendations from the most important NET societies for prevention and treatment remain inconsistent, and available evidence is still fragmented. To address this gap, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, and Embase up to May 2025, with the aim of identifying, organizing, and critically appraising the existing evidence on prevention and therapeutic strategies for managing hormonal crises in patients undergoing PRRT. Twenty-eight studies were included, comprising 18 case reports/series, 7 retrospective studies, and 3 prospective studies. Reported events included carcinoid crisis, insulinoma-related hypoglycemia, VIPoma-related secretory crisis, ectopic Cushing syndrome exacerbation, and catecholaminergic crisis in pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma. Carcinoid crisis was the most frequently reported endocrine emergency, with available cohort studies suggesting an incidence ∼1% during PRRT, although definitions and reporting remain heterogeneous. Hypoglycemic crises occurred mainly during the first PRRT cycle in patients with insulinoma, supporting the role of inpatient monitoring and preventive glucose-stabilizing strategies. Evidence for rarer syndromes was limited to small series and case reports but consistently emphasized pretreatment endocrine optimization, syndrome-specific prophylaxis, early recognition, and multidisciplinary management. Overall, available data remain insufficient to support firm recommendations but suggest that structured risk assessment, periprocedural monitoring, and harmonized management algorithms are essential to improve PRRT safety in functioning NETs.

candidates.title: Machine learning quantifies within-subject facial change in acromegaly.
candidates.abstract: Machine-learning models can distinguish acromegaly from controls in single photographs, but whether gradual facial change can be measured within the same person from ordinary photographs is unknown. We tested whether a person's face shifts measurably toward an acromegaly-associated pattern over time. Multicenter, international, cross-sectional cohort study with within-subject longitudinal analysis. People with acromegaly and other pituitary neuroendocrine tumours contributed retrospective photographs. Two timepoints per person were paired by self-reported disease stage when available, with chronological pairing otherwise. A face-recognition model and a general-image model described each image, and leave-one-patient-out scoring quantified within-person movement toward the acromegaly-associated pattern. Of 582 participants, 110 contributed usable frontal photographs and 69 had 2 timepoints (50 acromegaly, 19 tumour controls). The facial score separated held-out advanced disease from control faces (AUC 0.858). In acromegaly, the median within-person shift was 0.59 and 76.0% moved in the predicted direction (P = .0003); 81.5% of clean untreated pairs moved as predicted (P = .0008). The 3 contrast strata ordered directionally, although the trend was not significant (P = .15). The 15 non-Cushing aging controls showed no significant shift (P = .72), and the between-group difference remained after adjustment for photograph interval (P = .029). Prediagnosis untreated baselines showed modest separation from all control baselines (AUC 0.65, 1-sided P = .033). The general-image model showed no within-person change (P = .32). Acromegaly-associated facial change is measurable within individuals from ordinary photographs, supporting further evaluation of longitudinal photograph-based monitoring and earlier recognition.

candidates.title: Etiological Roles Are Not Fixed: A Functional-Temporal and Adaptive-Capacity Framework for Painful Temporomandibular Disorders.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Painful temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are multifactorial and biopsychosocial, yet identifying associated factors does not establish the function each factor occupies along an individual clinical trajectory. This conceptual hypothesis article aimed to propose a functional-temporal framework that distinguishes etiological role from biopsychosocial domain and incorporates individual adaptive capacity. Methods: The framework was developed from established TMD concepts and purposively selected prospective and longitudinal evidence relevant to first onset, post-onset course, repeated measurement, and person-by-exposure interaction. The article is not a systematic or scoping review. Results: Recognized influences are organized into three functional positions: predisposing, initiating, and perpetuating. These positions are not treated as intrinsic properties of variables; assignment depends on temporal ordering, context, measurement, phenotype, and the specified outcome. Adaptive capacity is proposed as a conceptual source of differential response and is distinguished from generic effect modification, which is one empirical strategy for testing the hypothesis. Existing longitudinal studies show that susceptibility, onset-related change, post-onset course, and exposure-by-person interactions can be measured, but no cohort has validated the complete framework. Falsifiable predictions and conservative wording rules are specified. Conclusions: The framework offers a temporally disciplined approach to etiological interpretation and patient communication without implying deterministic causation or treatment efficacy. Its current empirical basis is strongest for painful TMD, and densely measured inception cohorts are needed to test whether functional position and prespecified moderators add explanatory or predictive information.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: Sinonasal and Olfactory Quality of Life Following Endonasal Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Triphasic Recovery Analysis in Ethiopia.
candidates.abstract: To characterize the sinonasal and olfactory quality of life (QoL) trajectory. A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted on 91 patients undergoing TSS at Addis Ababa University teaching hospitals between May 2024 and August 2025. QoL was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) questionnaire v4 preoperatively and at 3- and 6-month postoperatively. Analysis revealed a characteristic triphasic recovery pattern: low preoperative baseline, a transient peak in morbidity at 3 months, and an improvement toward baseline by 6 months for most systemic domains. At 3 months, significant score worsening occurred for loss of smell/taste (mean: 1.7, p < 0.001), thick discharge (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), congestion (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), postnasal discharge (mean: 0.7, p < 0.001), and runny nose (mean: 0.5, p = 0.003). By 6 months, persistence was confined to loss of smell/taste (p < 0.001), thick discharge (p < 0.001), and congestion (p = 0.005). Exploratory analysis in the nasoseptal flap cohort (n = 3) showed higher scores. Preliminary findings of delayed ear pain/fullness in acromegaly at 6 months hypothesized to reflect a link between growth hormone normalization and altered Eustachian tube function. Poorer sleep with binostril access (p = 0.017) speculatively associated with bilateral synechiae under limited postoperative care. Unlike Western cohorts, protracted recovery may reflect lack of standardized high-volume saline irrigation and scheduled debridement. TSS demonstrates a favorable long-term QoL profile; however, localized sinonasal and olfactory deficits often persist at 6 months.

candidates.title: The Digital Renaissance of Customized Subperiosteal Implants-Clinical Outcomes, Surgical Workflow, and Current Evidence for the Rehabilitation of Severely Atrophic Jaws: A Narrative Review.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rehabilitation of the severely atrophic edentulous jaw remains one of the most demanding challenges in oral and maxillofacial reconstruction, particularly when extensive bone augmentation is contraindicated, has previously failed, or is refused by the patient. Subperiosteal implants, first introduced in the 1940s and largely abandoned due to poor long-term performance, have re-emerged over the past decade as a viable alternative through the integration of cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-based virtual planning, computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM), and additive manufacturing. This review summarizes current evidence on the clinical outcomes, surgical workflow, and indications of customized, digitally designed subperiosteal implants. Materials and Methods: A structured literature search was performed in PubMed and Scopus, supplemented by manual searching, to identify publications relevant to the predefined clinical and conceptual scope of this narrative review. Search terms addressed subperiosteal implants, digital/CAD-CAM workflows, additive manufacturing, severe jaw atrophy, and clinical outcomes. Predefined selection criteria were applied to maintain consistency with the scope of the review, and the literature-selection process was documented using a descriptive flow diagram. Results: Sixty-two publications were retained as the core literature informing the narrative synthesis, comprising systematic reviews and meta-analyses, retrospective and multicenter clinical studies, case series, case reports, and biomechanical/technical investigations. The synthesized evidence indicates short-to-medium-term implant survival generally exceeding 90%, with soft-tissue exposure and dehiscence as the most frequently reported complications, and a decline in survival on longer follow-up. Digitally designed subperiosteal implants are increasingly reported for severely resorbed maxillae and mandibles, oncologic and post-traumatic defects, syndromic patients, and cases of failed conventional or zygomatic implant therapy. Conclusions: Digital workflows have renewed clinical interest in subperiosteal implants by enabling patient-specific design and digitally supported planning and manufacturing. However, the evidence base remains dominated by case reports and heterogeneous retrospective series, underscoring the need for prospective, standardized, long-term studies.

candidates.title: Comparison of demographic, clinical and follow-up data of patients with micromegaly and acromegaly: a retrospective analysis from a single tertiary center.
candidates.abstract: Micromegaly is a term suggested to describe patients with clinical and biochemical evidence of acromegaly despite apparently normal GH secretion. However, its clinical characteristics including biochemical definition, treatment outcomes, and long-term prognosis remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of micromegaly and compare the demographic, clinical, biochemical, radiological, and long-term follow-up characteristics of patients with micromegaly and classical acromegaly. A retrospective chart review was conducted in patients with acromegaly, who were diagnosed and subsequently followed up in Erciyes University Department of Endocrinology between January 2010 and September 2025. Micromegaly was defined on the basis of the finding of a baseline growth hormone (GH) < 2 ng/mL and/or glucose-suppressed GH nadir < 1 ng/mL, in addition to an IGF-1 level above the upper limit of normal in a patient with the classic symptoms and signs of the disease. Among 117 patients with acromegaly, 14 (12%) were classified as having micromegaly. No statistically significant differences were observed in the age at diagnosis, gender distribution, comorbidities and clinical symptoms between patients with acromegaly and micromegaly. The micromegaly group demonstrated a higher incidence of microadenoma, with a significantly smaller maximal tumor size compared to the acromegaly group. The rate of surgical intervention, the total number of operations, and the rate of additional medical treatment among patients with acromegaly were significantly higher than among patients with micromegaly. The biochemical control rate observed at 3 months postoperatively was higher in the micromegaly group, while the remission rate at the last visit was similar between the two groups. Patients classified as having micromegaly according to the biochemical criteria applied in this study exhibited clinical manifestations and comorbidity profiles comparable to those of patients with classical acromegaly despite lower GH levels and smaller tumors. Sensitivity analyses using alternative biochemical definitions demonstrated a broadly consistent overall clinical pattern across the different classification approaches. These findings suggest that apparently low GH secretion does not necessarily indicate clinically mild disease. Prospective multicentre studies using standardized biochemical definitions are required to further clarify the biological basis and clinical significance of micromegaly. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Newly Diagnosed Graves' Disease Followed by the Discovery of a Cavernous Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm Causing Panhypopituitarism: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sellar and parasellar vascular lesions are rare causes of pituitary dysfunction and may mimic pituitary adenomas or other sellar masses. Cavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) aneurysms can cause hypopituitarism through compression of the pituitary gland or stalk, but diagnosis may be delayed when symptoms are initially attributed to a more common endocrine disorder. We report a 37-year-old man who presented with six weeks of unintentional weight loss, fatigue, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, anxiety, tremor, and tachycardia. Initial evaluation showed suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated total triiodothyronine (T3), positive thyrotropin receptor antibody, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin, and a hypervascular thyroid gland on ultrasound, consistent with Graves' disease. He was started on methimazole and atenolol. Although thyroid function tests improved, he developed persistent neck discomfort, prompting contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), which revealed an enhancing sellar mass. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a T2-hypointense sellar lesion with internal flow artifact, and CT angiography confirmed a saccular aneurysm of the cavernous segment of the right ICA. Pituitary hormone evaluation demonstrated secondary adrenal insufficiency, central hypothyroidism, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, growth hormone (GH) deficiency, and mild hyperprolactinemia, consistent with panhypopituitarism from pituitary compression. The patient was started on prednisone and levothyroxine, and atenolol and prednisone were subsequently discontinued before endovascular embolization was performed. At follow-up, symptoms improved, but panhypopituitarism persisted. This case highlights the importance of reassessing patients when endocrine symptoms evolve despite an initially appropriate diagnosis.

candidates.title: Proteomic profiling of somatotropinoma subtypes reveals TNIP1 overexpression in sparsely granulated tumors in a small discovery cohort.
candidates.abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying the clinical differences between densely granulated (DG) and sparsely granulated (SG) somatotroph tumors remain poorly understood. To identify significant molecular differences between these subtypes, we performed quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling followed by validation of the differentially-identified proteins. Label-free quantitative proteomic analysis was performed on SG somatotroph adenomas (SGSAs, n = 3) and DG somatotroph adenomas (DGSAs, n = 3), with each sample analyzed in technical triplicate. Key findings were subsequently validated using immunohistochemistry (IHC, n = 64), immunofluorescence (IF, n = 24), and Western blotting (WB, n = 18). Proteomic profiling identified TNFAIP3-interacting protein 1 (TNIP1) as the most significantly over-expressed protein, and coenzyme Q6 monooxygenase (COQ6) as the most significantly under-expressed protein, in SGSAs compared with DGSAs. Higher TNIP1 expression in SGSAs was significantly associated with IGF-1 [%ULN], larger tumor diameter, greater tumor volume, higher Knosp grade and SSTR5 expression. In contrast, COQ6 expression showed significant negative correlations with tumor diameter, tumor volume, Knosp grade, and SSTR5 expression. These findings indicate strong associations between TNIP1 and COQ6 expression and tumor characteristics, along with differences in cell adhesion and signaling pathways. SGSAs and DGSAs exhibit distinct proteomic profiles. Increased TNIP1 and reduced COQ6 expression, together with alterations in cell adhesion and signaling pathways in SGSA, may contribute to the molecular and phenotypic differences underlying these somatotroph tumor subtypes.

candidates.title: The Impact of COVID-19 on African American Dental Students' Self-Confidence in Implementing Specific Clinical Treatments.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Few studies have examined the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on the clinical readiness of dental students in the provision of care. This study examined whether dental students who graduated during the pre-pandemic period (2019 and before) would have higher self-reported clinical skills confidence than those who graduated during the post-pandemic period (2025 and after) at the only two Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) in the United States that teach dentistry. The study hypothesized that the change in educational methods that resulted from the pandemic would result in a reduction in self-reported confidence during the senior year. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was sent to dental graduates from two Historically Black Colleges and Universities in the United States. The questionnaire included a validated 40-item instrument to measure self-reported confidence during senior year in clinical procedures and questions about relevant demographic variables. Results: In fixed prosthodontics, confidence decreased significantly for tooth preparation, impressions, try-in of ceramic-fused-to-metal restorations, and cementation of fixed prostheses (p < 0.05). Confidence also declined for diagnostic and periodontal procedures, including mucogingival anomaly diagnosis, surgical elimination of periodontal pockets, and management of traumatic dental contacts (p < 0.05). The largest decline was seen in the diagnosis and conservative treatment of oroantral communications and fistulas. Of particular clinical and statistical importance, there were significant reductions in self-confidence in the ability to perform tooth extractions and minor oral surgery in medically compromised patients, tooth extractions with separation of roots, and diagnosis and therapy of acute and chronic dental infections (p < 0.05). Conclusions: The findings provide further evidence of the adverse effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on the African American dental workforce. Given the limited access to care that patients traditionally treated by HBCU dentists have, this study provides evidence that the underserved community may be more adversely affected by the pandemic than previously described.

candidates.title: Non-Metal Primary Crowns in Telescopic and Double-Crown Systems Involving Natural Teeth: A Scoping Review.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: This scoping review mapped clinical, in vitro, and in silico evidence on non-metal primary crowns in telescopic and double-crown systems involving natural teeth, including retention, wear, mechanical behavior, clinical outcomes, and auxiliary retention-control elements. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Dentistry & Oral Sciences Source through EBSCO, and Web of Science were searched for English-language reports published from 2015 onward. These limits and the exclusion of case reports were predefined in a written, unregistered protocol. Elicit provided supplementary citation discovery, and a targeted backward reference-list check was performed using the same eligibility criteria. Findings and extractable numerical retention outcomes were charted descriptively without formal critical appraisal or quantitative pooling. Results: Forty-eight reports were included, 40 in vitro, one in silico, and seven clinical reports, representing six identifiable cohorts. Two clinical reports arose from the same randomized cohort. The backward reference-list check identified nine additional eligible reports. Clinical evidence was concentrated on zirconia primary crowns with electroformed or electroplated gold secondaries, although two additional short-term trials evaluated zirconia with polymeric secondary structures. Retention varied with the complete material and design combination. Four laboratory reports examined auxiliary retention-control concepts; no clinical study isolated their effects. Conclusions: Clinical evidence remains very limited. Polymeric primary crowns and auxiliary retention-control elements were represented mainly by laboratory evidence. Retention should be interpreted as a system-level outcome. Mixed-support outcomes require support-specific interpretation, and this review does not establish comparative clinical superiority.

candidates.title: Fracture Resistance and Stress Distribution of Weakened Bovine Roots Restored with Different Glass Fiber Post Systems.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: The restoration of structurally weakened roots remains a clinical challenge. This in vitro study evaluated the fracture resistance, failure pattern, and stress distribution of weakened bovine roots restored with two glass fiber post systems under different remaining root dentin thicknesses. Methods: Sixty bovine incisor roots were divided into six groups (n = 10): G1, 2 mm of remaining root dentin without a post; G2, 3 mm without a post; G3, 2 mm with an Exacto post; G4, 3 mm with an Exacto post; G5, 2 mm with a Splendor-SAP post; and G6, 3 mm with a Splendor-SAP post. Specimens underwent root canal treatment and standardized restoration, followed by 1,200,000 mechanical cycles at 88 N and 3.8 Hz and fracture testing at 45°. Finite element models were subjected to an 88 N oblique load. Fracture resistance was analyzed using Welch's one-way ANOVA followed by Games-Howell post hoc comparisons, whereas failure patterns were analyzed using the Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. Results: Fracture resistance differed significantly among groups (p < 0.001). G1 (88.7 N) and G2 (95.6 N) showed the lowest and statistically similar values; G3 (670.9 N) and G5 (691.9 N) showed intermediate and statistically similar values; and G4 (786.2 N) and G6 (784.8 N) showed the highest and statistically similar values. Failure-pattern distribution was not significantly associated with the experimental groups (p = 0.582). Finite element analysis showed stress concentration predominantly in the cervical region of the root, with G5 showing the highest maximum principal stress in root dentin. Conclusions: Glass fiber posts substantially increased the fracture resistance of weakened roots. Among post-restored specimens, roots with 3 mm of remaining dentin showed higher fracture resistance than those with 2 mm, whereas no significant difference was observed between the Exacto and Splendor-SAP systems under the same remaining-dentin condition.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.
